actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Seed of the environment's random generator
inputs.name: seed

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

device.name: NSMR Nsmr-v1 (2D mobile robot navigation simulator)

facts.text: Nsmr-v1 is registered with entry_point nsmr.envs.NsmrGymEnv:NsmrGymEnv and max_episode_steps=500
The observation space is a Dict of a lidar Box with num_range elements from min_range to max_range and a target Box with bounds [0.0, -1.0, -1.0] to [100.0, 1.0, 1.0]

The action space is a Box of two values, linear velocity between min_linear_velocity and max_linear_velocity and angular velocity between min_angular_velocity and max_angular_velocity, both read from the robot configuration
The bundled robot configuration sets radius 0.3, linear velocity limits 0.0 and 1.0, and angular velocity limits -1.0 and 1.0
The bundled robot configuration sets linear acceleration 0.5 and angular acceleration 1.0
The bundled lidar configuration has 720 rays, range 0.1 to 30.0, max_angle 1.5707963267948966 and angle_increment 0.004363323129985824
NsmrGymEnv constructs NSMR with only robot and layout
NSMR's constructor default timestep is dt=0.1 s and it is stored as the simulator's DT
NSMR.update runs add_bias, stuck, check_action, state_transition and add_noise in that order
check_action limits the change of each velocity by max_linear_acceleration*DT or max_angular_acceleration*DT and then clamps both to the robot's velocity limits
state_transition integrates the unicycle pose in closed form and normalizes the heading
reset_pose draws a random pose until it is collision free and a random target
reset_noise_param draws the noise parameters from numpy's global random module
get_lidar returns num_range readings from the Raycasting map, with oversight and range noise

The reward is goal_reward when the distance is below the robot radius, -collision_penalty on a collision and otherwise alpha times the distance change; a stop_penalty is subtracted when there is no progress, and beta/(2*pi)*abs(theta) for the heading error
is_done is true at max_steps, on a collision or after the goal
reset returns only the observation and step returns the legacy 4-tuple (observation, reward, done, info)

determinism.notes: the fake draws its start pose and target from Python's random.Random(seed), so one seed repeats its trajectory; the upstream NsmrGymEnv.seed only assigns self.np_random while NSMR draws from numpy's global random module (nsmr.py:61-69, 107-108, 148-150, 168), so the upstream simulator itself is not reproducible from the seed

gaps: kinematic 2D unicycle only: no rigid-body dynamics, contacts or collision forces; is_collision (nsmr.py:129-137) is an occupancy lookup and outside the map it returns false

the fake does not raycast the 10 m x 10 m map (simple_map.json:2-3, 1000 cells at 0.01 m): it returns the real 720 lidar values (robot.json:18) as placeholder readings all at max_range, so its observations are not the upstream's
the fake does not model the upstream sensor and actuator noise, the stuck state or the lidar oversight events (nsmr.py:100-124, 148-150); its trajectories are not compared with the upstream's
no rendering: the fake's render returns None and the upstream Renderer is not reimplemented
the reward follows the upstream default parameters, but the fake does not model collisions and detects a goal only from the distance
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state or set_state
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, only commands advance simulated time (100 ms per tick)
no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against one

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
